issues.description: The problem statement UML (and the solution) specify a Stock method named emptyStock(): void, but the template Stock implementation provides a method named clearInventory() instead. This name mismatch is structural: students following the specification or the solution will expect Stock.emptyStock() to exist and may call it, which will cause compilation errors or test failures with the provided template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the specification and solution by renaming clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or add a public emptyStock() method that delegates to clearInventory(). Ensure the template and problem statement consistently use the same method name.

issues.description: The Stock class method that clears the inventory is named differently across artifacts: the problem statement (and the solution) expect a method named emptyStock(), but the template Stock.java provides clearInventory(). This mismatch can confuse students who look for emptyStock() as specified in the task and UML, and may cause difficulties implementing or calling the expected API.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() to match the problem statement and solution. Alternatively, add a new emptyStock() method in the template that invokes clearInventory() so both names are supported and students can follow the UML specification.
